newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia Cilacap visbreaker faces start up delay.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Cilacap visbreaker faces start up delay.

text.p: A 55,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) visbreaker at Indonesia's Cilacap refinery is facing start up problems which might result in state-owned Pertamina allocating more low sulphur waxy residue for October export, refinery sources said on Wednesday.
The visbreaker was closed for a one-month maintenance in September along with the 200,000-bpd crude distillation and other related secondary units.
The CDU and other units restarted operations on October 7.

The first attempt to restart the visbreaker was made on October 2 but failed bacause of power supply problems. The second attempt was made on October 4 and the third attempt was on October 6, the sources said.
The third attempt initially succeeded in cracking naphtha out of the LSWR but the unit faced problems with its filter and was forced to shut again for cleaning operations, they said.
The sources said the refinery will try to restart the visbreaker again on October 10 and they expect the unit to function normally by then at the earliest.
LSWR is fed into a visbreaker and cracked into naphtha and distillates. About 30-35 percent of the LSWR is processed into light and middle distillates while the rest remained as residues.
The sources said, as a result of the delay in start up, the LSWR feedstock has to be stored in tankers.
Traders said this might force Pertamina to sell more prompt LSWR.
Pertamina allocated 3.8 million barrels of LSWR for October lifting to be exported.
